title: Evictless prefetch adapter and scheduler streamline for lower tail latency
creator: Maya Patel
description: Reduce CPU stalls and tail latency caused by KV cache eviction storms and complex scheduler handoffs. This ticket decomposes the monolithic batch lifecycle into a small 'prefetch adapter' that drives KV warmups without touching eviction heuristics, and a lean scheduler cleanup that removes cross-thread synchronous handoffs. The goal is to: 1) eliminate short lived blocking during request admission, 2) reduce KV eviction-induced cache churn for hot prefix workloads, and 3) simplify the scheduler handoff path to reduce 95th/99th percentile latency for short requests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 95th token-latency for <128 token requests decreases by >=12% on our staging workload compared to baseline from 2026-01-01. 2) KV eviction rate for hot prefix keys reduces by >=30% under the same load. 3) No increase in overall token cost >2%. 4) All unit, integration, and perf tests pass in CI and a canary rollout completes on 'canary-2' without regressions after 24h.
implementation_notes: Plan: (A) Introduce a prefetch adapter interface that subscribes to admission events and enqueues KV warmup tasks into the existing async prefetch pool. The adapter will be eviction-aware and mark warmed keys with a short soft-lease to avoid immediate eviction. (B) Replace synchronous cross-thread handoffs in scheduler with an MPSC token queue + lightweight token steward that batches lease updates every 2ms. (C) Add adaptive backpressure: when prefetch queue length > threshold we drop prefetch for low-priority requests. (D) Upgrade tokio from 1.12 -> 1.16 to take advantage of improved task scheduling; pin bytes crate to 1.2.x to avoid regressing memory fragmentation. Rollout: feature-flagged behind runtime.prefetch_eviction_safe and staged canary on canary-1 (10% traffic) -> canary-2 (50%) -> full.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: new prefetch lease markers could prevent legitimate evictions under memory pressure leading to OOM. Mitigation: implement a global soft-lease budget and fall back to LRU-driven eviction when memory headroom < 12%. Risk: tokio upgrade surfaces subtle timing changes. Mitigation: run extended soak on canary-2 for 48h and run stress tests that simulate 10x short-request traffic bursts.
test_plan: Unit tests for adapter contract and lease markers. Integration: end-to-end with synthetic workloads (hot-prefix, long-streaming, mixed) using perf harness. Perf: A/B tests against baseline measuring p50/p95/p99 token latency, KV eviction rate, CPU utilization, and token cost. Canary: staged rollout with automated rollback if p95 increases >5% or eviction rate increases >10%.
